meta.verifiedAgainst: <fleet checkout> — re-verify with scripts/check-fleet-contract.mjs against your fleet checkout
meta.description: Machine-readable contract between Deal Onboarding and the fleet task API. Deal Onboarding is the consumer and owns this fixture: scripts/check-fleet-contract.mjs diffs every fact against a fleet checkout (and, optionally, the runner bundle that carries the MCP catalog + personas). Facts noted asserted-not-extracted are listed as documented residuals, never silently skipped.

api.estimateTaskNote: Deal Onboarding's connection check (GET /api/runner/check -> runner.Client.Check) POSTs here. EstimateTask shares authorizeTaskCreator with CreateTask/CreateTasksBatch (batch.go) so the creation-shaped endpoints cannot drift apart, and is read-only by construction ("the forecast creates nothing, so this cannot become a weaker path to task creation") - so it verifies a scoped create_task key without booking anything. Authorization runs BEFORE readJSON, which is why Deal Onboarding treats any non-401/403 (including a 400 on its minimal probe body) as key-accepted. It reuses the TaskCreate wire shape already pinned in taskCreate, so it adds no new request-schema coupling.
api.apiInfoUnauthenticatedNote: /api-info is served OUTSIDE the auth middleware (fleet internal/httpapi/server.go registers it on the bare mux; internal/apiversion.unversionedForever lists it beside the health probes). Deal Onboarding's connection check relies on this to separate "host unreachable" from "host up, key rejected" - if fleet ever puts it behind auth, the check must stop reporting an auth failure as unreachable.
api.uploadScopedKeyNote: fleet#719 SHIPPED (verified 2026-08-31, internal/sched/handlers/upload.go): POST /v1/upload now validates a scoped key against PermissionCreateTask - "the SAME scoped keys that may create tasks may stage uploads - an external front-door app no longer needs the full-access admin key just to attach a brief." A valid-but-under-scoped typed key gets a definitive 403 (#190 semantics). The Deal Onboarding deployment may therefore hold a least-privilege create_task key even for attachment-bearing creates; it no longer needs an admin key.
api.unknownFieldsNote: fleet's readJSON is a plain json.Decoder without DisallowUnknownFields: additive fields Deal Onboarding sends early (serialization_key) are ACCEPTED and silently discarded rather than rejected. Safe for additive-first evolution, but it means a missing feature fails silently — which is exactly why serializationKeyHonored below is pinned.

taskCreate.serializationKeyNote: fleet#709 SHIPPED (verified 2026-08-31): serialization_key is a real TaskCreate field (internal/sched/models/models.go), persisted on Task, and ENFORCED at claim time - internal/sched/db/claim.go acquireSerializationLockTx + hasActiveTaskWithSerializationKeyTx refuse to claim a task while another task with the same key is active. The <=1-active-task-per-key mutual exclusion therefore holds on fleet.
taskCreate.duplicateFileNameNote: fleet 400s a create whose file_names carry duplicates — Deal Onboarding dedupes logical names client-side (uniqueLogicalName, files.ts) and reserves deal_brief.json for the structured brief (#282.2).

credentialAllowlist.note: fleet Gate-3 semantics (internal/agentcore/credential_allowlist.go): a POPULATED allowlist permits ONLY the listed (server, account) pairs — every other MCP call returns the denialMarker as a tool-level error at the broker, even after mcp_load_servers. Deal Onboarding therefore puts EVERY pair a run must call on the list: the batch's SSP servers (variant-routed pairs keep their account slug, default-seat pairs are accountless) plus deal_sheet + sendgrid (#279).

taskUrl.note: The trader-facing task view fleet's own notifications link to (internal/runner/notify.go). BaseURL + /tasks/{id} is the auth-gated JSON API route and must never be surfaced to traders (#282.1).

persona.note: No persona ships with Deal Onboarding. Set RUNNER_PERSONA to a persona your runner bundle defines (personas/<name>.yaml); leave blank to let the runner use its default. When set here, the checker verifies the file exists in the supplied bundle.

mcpServers.note: Server names Deal Onboarding routes deals to. Ground truth is your runner bundle catalog (manifest.yaml under the bundle root, verified when the checkout is supplied); the frontend SSP_SERVER map, the Go sspServerByKey map, and the Go defaultFleetMCPServers roster are all pinned to this table.
